story: Indra, king of the gods and lord of thunder, killed the serpent Vritra, who had trapped the world's waters, and is the most praised god of the Rigveda. He rules heaven from his city Amaravati and rides the white elephant Airavata.
belief: In Vedic times Indra was the chief god, prayed to for rain and victory. Today he is seen more as a powerful but flawed ruler of heaven than as a god of personal devotion.
turns: Insecure about his throne, he kept sending celestial dancers to break the penance of sages. He seduced Ahalya disguised as her husband and was cursed by the sage Gautama. When he flooded Gokul out of pride, Krishna lifted a hill against him and ended his worship there.
facts: About a quarter of the Rigveda's hymns are addressed to him.
His weapon, the vajra, was made from the bones of the sage Dadhichi, who gave his life for it.
